rules.label: Free care (<=100% FPL)
rules.quote: Patients whose family income is at or below 100% of the FPL are eligible to receive free care.

rules.label: Up to 50% discount (100-150% FPL)
rules.quote: Patient whose family income is over 100% and below 150% of the FPL would be eligible for up to a 50% discount.

rules.label: Case-by-case discounted rates (>150% FPL)
rules.quote: Patients whose family income exceeds 150% of the FPL may be eligible to receive discounted rates on a case-by-case basis based on their specific circumstances, such as catastrophic illness or medical indigence, at the discretion of Community Hospital; however, the discounted rates shall not be greater than the amounts generally billed commercially insured patients.

application.quote: Accounts turned to bad debt remain eligible for financial assistance consideration as long as the complete application and documentation are submitted prior to 240 days from the date of the initial account statement;

eca_not_before.quote: ECA’s will not be initiated by Community Hospital or by an outside collection agency acting on behalf of Community Hospital until at least 120 days after the initial guarantor account statement has been mailed.

payment_plan.quote: For patients who qualify for charity and who are cooperating in good faith to resolve their discounted hospital bills, Community Hospital may offer extended payment plans, will not send unpaid bills to outside collection agencies, and will cease all collection efforts

notes: The policy states that financial assistance benefits are provided as a last resort and all other payment options must be explored first.
The policy excludes non-urgent services from financial assistance at the hospital's discretion.
Elective procedures and flat rate procedures including cosmetic, bariatric lithotripsy are not eligible for charity care.
Complications due to elective procedures are considered on a case-by-case basis by hospital leadership.
The hospital reserves the right to reevaluate eligibility if there is a change in income during the benefit period or when hospital care is required to determine eligibility for other aid.
Benefits under the program will not exceed twelve months.
Applicants have 30 days to appeal a denial in writing with the Business Office Manager.
Applicants must provide required information within 14 days of the application date or risk denial.
Misrepresentation or falsification of information will cause financial assistance to be withdrawn retroactively and currently.
Relatives or guardians may apply for an incapacitated or deceased individual.
Gross personal and business income will be used to determine eligibility, consistent with CICP program guidelines.
Income for all members of the household and legally responsible parties not in the household will be considered.
The hospital will provide an itemized statement showing charges and discount amount applied after a complete application is submitted.
The determination may be done at any point in the collection cycle and re-evaluated if the last evaluation was over a year prior or new relevant information arises.
Patients must submit documentation including last year's tax return, last three months' income, or bank statements for proof of income and account balances.
Requests for charity are processed promptly and applicants are notified in writing within 30 days of receipt of a completed application.
In the absence of a financial assistance form, the hospital may use outside agencies to estimate income for eligibility determination.
For patients cooperating in good faith, the hospital will not impose extraordinary collection actions without first making reasonable efforts to determine charity eligibility.
Reasonable efforts include validating the debt, identifying third-party payments, offering charity application opportunities, and offering payment plans.
Extraordinary collection actions include wage garnishments, liens on primary residences, and other legal actions.
If a collection agency identifies financial assistance eligibility, collection activity is suspended and the application is reviewed.
If the entire balance is adjusted, the account is returned; if partial adjustment occurs and the patient fails to cooperate or is ineligible, collection resumes.
The hospital complies with all applicable federal, state, and local laws.
